definition: Where a body is, given as a distance and a direction from a chosen origin; a vector, measured in metres.
The change in a body's position, a vector from where it started to where it finished, whatever path it took.
The total length of the path a body travels, a scalar that never decreases, however often the body changes direction.
The rate of change of a body's position, a vector in $\text{m s}^{-1}$ that gives both how fast it moves and which way.
The rate at which a body covers distance, a scalar in $\text{m s}^{-1}$; instantaneous speed is the size of the instantaneous velocity.
The rate of change of a body's velocity, a vector in $\text{m s}^{-2}$; it can change the speed, the direction or both, and a negative value does not by itself mean slowing down.
The steepness of a graph, the change in the vertical quantity divided by the change in the horizontal quantity; the gradient of a tangent gives the rate of change at one point.
